The authors analyzed 96 stealth CMEs, 150 front-side CMEs associated with solar activity (FSCME with LCS), and 533 total CMEs observed from 2008-2014.
The average linear projected speed of stealth CMEs was 399 km/s, compared to 530 km/s for FSCME with LCS and 444 km/s for all CMEs.
The average kinetic energy of stealth CMEs was 26x10^29 erg, compared to 130x10^29 erg for FSCME with LCS and 62x10^29 erg for all CMEs.
The average central position angle (CPA) of stealth CMEs was 149°, compared to 174° for FSCME with LCS and 177° for all CMEs.
The average angular size of stealth CMEs was 84°, compared to 129° for FSCME with LCS and 103° for all CMEs.
The average mass of stealth CMEs was 16x10^13 g, compared to 36x10^13 g for FSCME with LCS and 22x10^13 g for all CMEs.
The average angle φ between the CME motion and the Sun-Earth line was 28° for stealth CMEs, 37° for FSCME with LCS, and 94° for all CMEs.
The average angle λ between the CME motion direction and the ecliptic plane was 27° for stealth CMEs, 33° for FSCME with LCS, and 29° for all CMEs.
The relative frequency of stealth CMEs peaked in 2011 around the solar minimum, while the relative frequency of FSCME with LCS had a broader peak in 2012.
For most CMEs in all groups, the rate of change of the angle φ with distance from the Sun was between -2°/Rs and 2°/Rs, where Rs is the solar radius.

The stealth CMEs identified in this study had higher average values for parameters like speed, kinetic energy, angular size, and mass compared to the stealth CMEs analyzed in the D'Huys et al. (2014) study.
The authors used a multi-step process to identify stealth CMEs, including matching observations from multiple coronagraphs and excluding CMEs associated with solar flares or filament eruptions.
The authors compared the kinematic and physical characteristics of stealth CMEs, front-side CMEs associated with solar activity, and all CMEs observed during the 2008-2014 period.
The authors found that stealth CMEs had the lowest average values for parameters like speed, kinetic energy, mass, and angular size compared to the other CME groups.
The authors discussed the distributions of CME properties like speed, acceleration, and energy for the different CME groups.
